newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Banks keep Brussels bourse alive ahead U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Banks keep Brussels bourse alive ahead U.S. data.

text.p: Interest in banks and other financial issues kept the Brussels bourse alive in thin Tuesday morning trade ahead of the release of U.S. economic indicators, dealers said.
"Apart from the banks, there's nothing going on. There's very low volume," one trader said.

The limited demand kept the Bel-20 leading stock index .BFX hovering just below its all-time record high of 2,233.65, set last week. At around 0900 GMT, the Bel-20 was at 2,229.71 points, up 0.57 percent on the day. But dealers were confident the record was for taking if U.S. data did not disappoint.
Financial markets are waiting for a raft of U.S. data this week, including employment cost and durable goods figures today, to get a better picture of the pace of U.S. economic growth.

Dealers said, however, that if the data lessen fears of a U.S. rate rise, Belgian shares would remain firm at least until May 9, when the payment of the first dividends by banks and other stocks will knock around 18 points off the Bel-20 index.

One trader said the reason for the banks' strong performance could be investors buying ahead of the dividend season, but also noted ongoing merger speculation and market rumours of a forthcoming warrant issue on a basket of Belgian bank shares.
